result.final_text:
## What this letter says

You had a breast X-ray (mammogram) on 16 September 2026. The screening clinic needs you to come back for more tests. This is called a recall.

Being called back does not mean you have cancer. About 4 in 5 women who are called back do not have breast cancer.

At your appointment, you may have:
- More breast X-rays (mammograms)
- An ultrasound scan (a picture made by sound waves)
- A biopsy (a small sample of tissue)

You will usually get most of your results on the same day.

## What you need to do

1. Come to your appointment on 7 October 2026 at 11:00 at the Breast Assessment Clinic, Eastmoor Hospital.
2. Plan for the visit to take up to 4 hours.
3. If you cannot come, call 01632 960 733 as soon as possible.

## Dates and medicines

**Your mammogram:**
16 September 2026 — Breast X-ray (mammogram)

**Your appointment:**
7 October 2026 at 11:00 — Breast Assessment Clinic, Eastmoor Hospital

No medicines are listed in this letter.

## Questions to ask your doctor

- What tests might I have at this appointment?
- Will I get my results on the day of my appointment?
- What does it mean to be called back?

## When to get urgent help

The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
